threads.last_note: Stuck — the search_threads regex is O(n*m) on large thread stores. 50+ threads causes visible lag on every MCP call.
threads.narrative: Optimizing the search_threads tool in the MCP server. With 50+ threads the regex-based keyword matching in handleSearchThreads() takes 800ms+, which blocks the JSON-RPC event loop. Profiled and confirmed the bottleneck is the nested loop over threads × search terms. Tried pre-indexing but hit issues with stale index after merges.
failed_approaches: Built an in-memory inverted index on session start — worked for search but the index went stale after saveMemoryMerged() writes. Would need cache invalidation on every write path.
Tried switching to a single combined regex with alternation (term1|term2|term3) — faster but broke phrase matching and returned false positives on partial word matches.
threads.handoff_summary: The search bottleneck is in bin/mcp-server.js handleSearchThreads() around line 180. The current approach lowercases every field of every thread on each search call. A pre-computed search text per thread (built once on load, updated on write) would fix it without needing a full inverted index. The CLI search in bin/cli.js cmdThreads() has the same pattern and should get the same fix.

threads.narrative: Fixing the sticky-note merge driver to handle concurrent thread additions. When two branches each add a new thread, the merge driver treats the threads array as a text blob and produces a conflict or silently drops one thread. Need array-aware JSON merging that deduplicates by thread ID.
failed_approaches: Tried using JSON.parse on each side and concatenating arrays — works for additions but doesn't handle edits to the same thread (e.g., both sides update last_note on the same thread ID). Produces duplicate threads.

threads.narrative: Claude Code hooks fail silently on Windows. The session-start hook uses unix paths with forward slashes to resolve .sticky-note/ paths, which breaks on Windows. Additionally, the inject-context hook spawns `git blame` with a shell command that doesn't work in cmd.exe. Tried normalizing paths but broke Linux in the process.
failed_approaches: Replaced all path.join with forward-slash concatenation — fixed Windows but broke the git blame call on Linux where the path must match the repo-relative format exactly.
Tried using cross-spawn npm package to normalize shell execution — the hooks run in a constrained environment where node_modules from the project aren't available, only built-in Node modules.
threads.handoff_summary: The fix needs to use path.resolve() and path.sep consistently in all three hook files. The git blame call in inject-context.js line 45 needs to convert Windows backslashes to forward slashes ONLY for the git argument, not for the fs.readFile path. bin/cli.js init command should detect Windows and adjust the hooks.json command format (no shebang needed on Windows).

threads.last_note: Stuck — audit JSONL files grow unbounded and slow down git operations. A 2MB audit file adds 3+ seconds to every git status.
threads.narrative: The per-user audit JSONL files grow without limit. After a few weeks of active use, dbandaru.jsonl hit 2MB and git operations (status, diff, add) became noticeably slower because the file is tracked. Tried rotation but the pre-commit hook auto-stages all audit files, so rotated-out files still get committed.
failed_approaches: Implemented log rotation (keep last 500 lines, archive the rest) — but the pre-commit hook stages .sticky-note/audit/*.jsonl which picks up the archive files too. Moving archives outside .sticky-note/ breaks the audit trail query.

Tried adding a max-lines config to sticky-note-config.json and truncating on write — this loses audit history silently, and the truncation races with concurrent writes from multiple hooks firing in the same session.
threads.handoff_summary: Best approach is probably: (1) add a configurable max_audit_lines to sticky-note-config.json, (2) on session close only, trim the JSONL to the last N entries, (3) update the pre-commit hook glob to exclude archive files (.sticky-note/audit/*.archive.jsonl). The trim should happen in the session-end hook, not on every write, to avoid the race condition.

profile where the time is going
the audit jsonl files are huge — try rotating them
rotation doesn't help because the pre-commit hook stages everything
